text:
jin: Quick sync: following the offload RFC, I want to propose a lightweight stochastic evictor that uses a logistic/CDF curve instead of hard thresholds. Goal: smooth eviction, reduce synchronized thrash, and make tenant fairness explicit.
riley: Short version pls.
jin: Instead of watermarks we compute a compact hotness score h in [0,1] per allocation (recentness, freq, size penalty, and rehydration cost estimate). We transform h via a sigmoid-like CDF (or small piecewise-linear curve) to get eviction probability p(h). Under severe memory pressure we fall back to deterministic reclaim.
devon: How expensive is this per access? last time we hit CPU in p99.
jin: Design constraints: per-access must be O(1) cheap updates (u8 counters + sampled increments). full score evaluation is batched every epoch. optional sample rate tunable.
anya: Can you sketch the metadata layout?
jin: Minimal meta: 6bytes target. e.g. {u8 recency; u8 freq; u8 size_bucket; u16 epoch_tag;} will fit in 64-bit or 96-bit aligned slot. Update hot path only touches two bytes usually.
riley: Show pseudocode for selection path.
jin: ```
// rough sketch
on_access(meta) { if (rand() % ACCESS_SAMPLE == 0) meta.recency = min(255, meta.recency + 1); if (rand() % FREQ_SAMPLE == 0) meta.freq = min(255, meta.freq + 1); }

compute_h(meta, size_est, rehyd_cost) { r = meta.recency/255.0; f = meta.freq/255.0; s = size_penalty(size_est); c = norm_rehyd(rehyd_cost); raw = a*r + b*f + c1*c - c2*s; return clamp((raw - shift) * scale, 0.0, 1.0); }

prob_evict = cdf_lookup(curve, h) * pressure_factor * tenant_scale;
if (rand01() < prob_evict && now > meta.cooldown_until) evict_and_mark_cooldown(meta);
```

devon: Tenant_scale? fairness model?
jin: Tenants have a configured weight w_i. We calculate tenant_scale = avg_w / clamp(w_i, min_w, max_w). Clamp prevents extreme amplification. Also provide a floor so small tenants don't get fully shielded.
anya: How do we estimate rehydrate cost? fetching KV cache to VRAM cost differs by model and sequence len.
jin: We'll use a running EWMA of observed rehydrate latency * tokens_generated_recently as a proxy (stored at tenant granularity). That cost factor biases eviction away from allocations that are expensive to rehydrate.
riley: Telemetry and alerting? we need to detect bad regressions quickly.
jin: Telemetry plan: per-tenant timeseries: evict_rate, rehydrate_miss_rate, post_evict_miss_latency, resident_ratio, churn. Add a replay harness that runs traces and measures GPU token-savings vs extra CPU cycles.
devon: Rollout strategy?
jin: Staged: 1) lab perf spike (1 week) -> microbench cost curve; 2) canary small set of synthetic tenants (1%) + a couple pilot customers (opt-in); 3) ramp to 10% after checks; 4) global with automatic kill-switch. Gates: 99p latency delta < 3% AND post-evict miss-rate delta < 8% AND net token-cost improvement positive.
anya: What about immediate re-fetch loops where we evict and the request immediately needs the page?
jin: Cooldown: after eviction mark allocation with cooldown ticks (proportional to past recency). Also add a small hysteresis by increasing sample_bias for recently-evicted allocations to avoid repeated re-pulls. Finally, if we detect short-term rehydrate bursts, temporarily lower pressure_factor globally for that tenant.
riley: Ops knobs? expose to console?
jin: Runtime flags for enable/disable, sample rates, cooling base, pressure_scale. In Console we expose sanitized sliders: probation window, tenant weight overrides, canary toggle, and experiment id for tracing.
devon: Any fallback semantics with existing watermark system?
jin: Yes: keep current deterministic watermarks for emergency reclaim. Stochastic path is used only when used_memory < emergency_threshold && > low_pressure_threshold. Emergency threshold still trumps.
anya: Who owns prototype + telem?
jin: I'll own prototype and lab perf harness. devon volunteers for cooldown/circuit breaker automation. riley will own telemetry dashboards and eval harness.
ninja-bot: Created task INF-4310: "stochastic-evictor-prototype" assigned to jin,riley,devon.
riley: Next action: PR gating checklist: perf numbers (CPU p50/p99), token cost delta, dashboard panels, canary automation runbook, and RFC follow-up doc. I'll draft the dashboard panels.
jin: I'll open an RFC follow-up with config schema and perf curves. Posting design doc draft later today.
anya: ok let's sync next Wed after spike.
jin: Thanks all. Keeping notes in the follow-up doc and perf job. :rocket:
